title: Car pulls when braking
h1: Why does my car pull to one side when I brake?
metaDesc: Car pulls left or right when you brake? See if it's a sticking caliper, tires or suspension, how urgent it is, and what to tell your mechanic.
synonyms: car pulls to the right when braking
car pulls to the left when braking
pulls to one side when stopping
car darts to one side under braking
car pulling when i hit the brakes
intro: A car should stop in a straight line. If it tugs left or right when you brake, one side may be braking harder than the other, or something in the steering or suspension may be shifting. Answer the questions below to see the likely causes and how soon it needs attention.
safety: If the brake pedal sinks toward the floor or feels soft, stop driving and have the car towed.
If the red brake warning light comes on while driving, pull over safely and don't continue.
If you see smoke or smell strong burning from a wheel, pull over and let it cool. Don't touch the wheel.

q_warning_signs.q: Along with the pull, do you notice any of these?
q_warning_signs.help: These signs tell us whether the brakes themselves are failing, which changes how urgent this is.

opts.a: The brake pedal feels soft, sinks, or the red brake warning light is on
A grinding or metal-on-metal scraping noise when I brake
A burning smell, or one wheel is much hotter than the others after a drive
The steering wheel shakes or the pedal pulses when I brake
None of these, it just pulls

q_when.q: Does the car also drift to one side when you're NOT braking?
q_when.help: In an empty parking lot at low speed, loosen your grip for a second. A steady tug to one side is not normal. Don't test this on a road; have a passenger or mechanic check it if you're not sure.

opts.a: Yes, it drifts a little even when cruising
No, it only pulls when I brake

q_tires.q: Check the tire pressures with a gauge when the tires are cold. What did you find?
q_tires.help: The correct pressures are on a sticker inside the driver's door jamb, not the number on the tire sidewall.

opts.a: One tire is noticeably lower than the rest
I haven't checked / I'm not sure
It started right after brake work or new tires
It always pulls the same way, and harder the harder I brake
I feel a clunk or shift when I first press the brake, then the pull
There's a wet, oily spot on the inside of one wheel or tire

result.title: The brake system may be losing pressure. Don't drive it
result.now: Park the car and have it towed, or call roadside assistance (your insurer, a motor club, or the number in your owner's manual).
if: If the brake fluid reservoir is low or you see fluid near a wheel, mention that to the shop. It points to a leak.
If the pedal still goes to the floor after pumping it, the brakes may not stop the car at all. Don't move it.
Topping up the brake fluid isn't a fix. Even if the level comes back up and you see no leak, have the brakes inspected before driving.
result.why: A soft or sinking pedal, or the red brake light, can mean the hydraulic system that pushes the brake pads isn't holding pressure. When one side loses pressure, the car pulls toward the side that's still braking, and full brake failure can follow.

causes.name: Brake fluid leak
causes.clues: Low fluid in the reservoir, or a wet spot near a wheel or under the car.
causes.against: A full reservoir and dry wheels make a leak less likely.

causes.name: Damaged brake hose or line
causes.clues: Rust on the metal lines, or a cracked or bulging rubber hose near one wheel.

causes.name: Failing master cylinder
causes.clues: The pedal slowly sinks while you hold it down at a stop, with no visible leak.

you: Look at the brake fluid level in the reservoir under the hood.
Look behind each wheel for wet, oily spots.

result.title: The brake pads on one side may be worn down to metal
result.now: Stop using the car and have it towed or call roadside assistance (your insurer, a motor club, or the number in your owner's manual). If the pads are down to metal, each stop makes the damage worse.
if: If the grinding only happens for the first few stops after rain or a car wash, it may be light surface rust. Have the brakes inspected anyway, since you also have a pull.
If the pedal also feels soft or sinks, treat it as a brake failure risk and don't move the car.
If you smell burning or see smoke from a wheel, keep clear and let it cool.
result.why: Grinding plus a pull usually means one side's pads are gone and metal is scraping on the rotor. That side brakes poorly and unevenly, so the car tugs and stopping distances get longer.

causes.name: Brake pads worn to the backing plate
causes.clues: A squeal for weeks that turned into grinding, or it's been a long time since the last brake job.

causes.name: Sticking caliper that wore one side's pads early
causes.clues: One wheel is dirtier with brake dust or hotter than the others.

causes.name: A stone or debris caught in the brake
causes.clues: The noise started suddenly, often after a gravel road.
causes.against: Debris usually makes a constant scraping, not just when braking.

you: Look through the wheel spokes at the pads. Very thin pads or shiny grooves in the rotor are bad signs.

result.title: One brake may be stuck on and dragging (a sticking caliper)
result.now: Pull over somewhere safe and let the brakes cool. Don't drive further until the brakes are checked. Have it towed or call roadside assistance (your insurer, a motor club, or the number in your owner's manual).
if: If you see smoke from a wheel, keep everyone clear and let it cool. Call 911 if you see flames.
If the brake pedal feels soft or sinks, or the red brake light comes on, don't move the car.
If the parking brake was partly on, release it fully and let everything cool. Overheated brakes can still be weakened, so have them checked before relying on the car.
result.why: A caliper squeezes the pads against the rotor. If its piston or slide pins stick, that brake drags or grabs unevenly, so the car pulls and the wheel gets very hot. Overheated brakes can fade and stop working well. A shop will usually check the slide pins, piston and hose before deciding which part to replace.

causes.name: Sticking caliper piston
causes.clues: One wheel is much hotter than the others, and that side has more brake dust.

causes.name: Seized caliper slide pins
causes.clues: Uneven wear between the inner and outer pad on the same wheel.

causes.name: Collapsed brake hose holding pressure
causes.clues: The drag gets worse after several stops and eases after the car sits.

you: Without touching, check whether one wheel is still giving off much more heat than the others. Don't drive just to test it.
Compare brake dust on the front wheels.
shop: Caliper piston and slide pin inspection
Wheel spin test with the car raised
Pad wear comparison side to side

result.title: Your brake discs may be worn uneven, causing both the shake and the pull (rotors)
result.now: Have the brakes inspected within the next few days. Until then, leave extra following distance and avoid hard braking from high speed.
if: If the shaking is getting worse quickly or you also hear grinding, get it checked within a day or two.
If one wheel is also hotter than the others, a sticking caliper may have damaged the rotor. Get it checked sooner.
If the pedal feels soft or sinks, you smell burning, or the red brake light comes on, stop driving and have it towed.
result.why: When a rotor's surface wears unevenly, the pads grab harder in some spots than others. You feel that as a pulsing pedal or shaking wheel, and if one side is worse the car can tug toward it. A shop will usually measure the rotors and check the calipers before deciding whether to resurface or replace them.

causes.name: Uneven rotor thickness or deposits
causes.clues: The shake is strongest when braking from highway speed.

causes.name: Sticking caliper overheating one rotor
causes.clues: One wheel runs hotter, or has more brake dust.

causes.name: Worn suspension or steering parts
causes.clues: Clunks over bumps, or the steering feels loose.

you: Notice whether the shake is in the steering wheel (usually front brakes) or the seat and pedal (often rear brakes).

result.title: Uneven tire pressure is a common, easy-to-fix cause of a pull
result.now: Check all four tires with a gauge when cold and set them to the pressures on the driver's door jamb sticker.
if: If the same tire is low again within a few days, it probably has a slow leak. Get it repaired soon.
If the pull is still there with correct pressures, have the alignment and brakes checked.
If the pedal feels soft, you hear grinding, or you smell burning from a wheel, don't keep driving. Have the brakes checked first.
result.why: A low tire has more drag and a different grip than the others, so the car drifts toward it, and braking makes that pull stronger. It's the quickest thing to rule out.

causes.name: Low pressure in one tire
causes.clues: One tire looks lower, or the tire pressure light has been on.

causes.name: Mismatched or unevenly worn tires
causes.clues: Different tire brands or tread depths on the same axle.

causes.name: Wheel alignment out of spec
causes.clues: The steering wheel sits off-center when driving straight.
causes.against: If correcting the pressure fixes it, alignment is less likely.

you: Check and set all tire pressures.
Compare tread depth and tire type left to right.

result.title: Possibly alignment or a tire issue, or a dragging brake
result.now: Book an alignment and brake inspection when convenient, ideally within a couple of weeks.
if: If one wheel feels much hotter than the others after a drive, a brake may be dragging. Get it checked within a day or two.
If the steering also feels loose or clunks over bumps, get it checked sooner.
If you smell burning or see smoke from a wheel, pull over, let it cool and don't drive further until it's checked.
If the pedal feels soft or the red brake light comes on, stop driving and have it towed.
result.why: A car that drifts while cruising and pulls harder when braking usually has a steady cause, like alignment or a tire problem, that braking makes more noticeable. A brake that's slightly dragging can do the same thing.

causes.name: Wheel alignment out of spec
causes.clues: A recent pothole or curb hit, or the steering wheel sits off-center.

causes.name: Tire problem (uneven wear or internal damage)
causes.clues: The pull changes if the front tires are swapped side to side.

causes.name: Dragging brake
causes.clues: One wheel is hotter or dustier than the other.

you: After a drive, compare how warm each wheel feels by holding your hand near it.
Look at the front tires for wear on just one edge.

result.title: Something from the recent work may need adjusting
result.now: Take it back to the shop that did the work within the next few days and tell them exactly when it pulls.
if: If the pedal feels soft or the pull is strong or sudden, don't drive it. Have the shop come to you or have it towed.
If new pads were installed, a slight pull for the first few dozen stops can happen while they bed in. If it doesn't fade, have it checked.
If you smell burning or one wheel is much hotter than the others, pull over, let it cool, and have it towed back rather than driven.
result.why: A pull that shows up right after brake or tire work is often linked to that work. Mismatched pads, a caliper not moving freely, air in the brake lines, or tires that differ side to side can all cause one side to brake differently. The shop that did the work will want to know and can usually recheck it quickly.

causes.name: Caliper or pads not installed or lubricated correctly
causes.clues: The pull started right after a brake job.

causes.name: Mismatched or new tires on one side
causes.clues: Only one or two tires were replaced, or tires were rotated.

causes.name: Air in the brake lines
causes.clues: The pedal feels softer than before the work.

you: Note which way it pulls and how hard you're braking when it happens.
Check the tire pressures.
shop: Brake bleed if the pedal is soft

result.title: One side may be braking harder than the other
result.now: Get the brakes inspected within the next few days. Until then, brake early and gently, and leave extra following distance.
if: If the pull suddenly gets stronger, the pedal changes, or you hear grinding, stop driving it and have it towed.
If one wheel is much hotter than the others after driving, a caliper may be sticking. Get it checked within a day or two, and don't drive it if there's a burning smell.
If the red brake light comes on or you see fluid near a wheel, stop driving and have it towed.
result.why: A consistent pull that grows with harder braking usually means the brakes on the left and right aren't gripping equally. The car pulls toward the side that's working better, so the other side may barely be braking.

causes.name: Sticking caliper or seized slide pins
causes.clues: Uneven brake dust or uneven pad wear between sides.

causes.name: Contaminated brake pads
causes.clues: A leak near one wheel, or recent work that may have left grease on the pads.

causes.name: Collapsed or blocked brake hose
causes.clues: The pull is worse after several stops in a row.

causes.name: Uneven tire pressure
causes.clues: One tire looks lower than the others.
causes.against: If the car doesn't drift at all when not braking, this is less likely.

you: Check tire pressures.
Compare the brake dust and wheel warmth on each side after a short drive.
shop: Brake inspection with pad and rotor measurement

result.title: Worn suspension or steering parts may be shifting when you brake
result.now: Have the suspension and steering inspected within the next few days. Avoid hard braking until then.
if: If the steering suddenly feels very loose, wanders a lot, or you hear a loud clunk followed by a change in steering, stop driving it and have it towed.
If the brake pedal feels soft or the red brake light comes on, stop driving and have it towed.
result.why: Braking shifts a lot of weight forward. If a control arm bushing, ball joint or tie rod is worn, the wheel can move out of position under that load. The clunk is the part shifting, and the pull follows.

causes.name: Worn control arm bushings
causes.clues: A clunk when you start braking, and the pull eases once the car settles.

causes.name: Worn ball joint or tie rod end
causes.clues: Clunks over bumps, loose-feeling steering, or uneven tire wear.

causes.name: Loose brake caliper mounting
causes.clues: A clunk at the moment you press or release the brake, at one wheel.

you: Note whether you hear clunks over bumps too.
Look at the front tires for wear on just one edge.
shop: Suspension and steering inspection with the wheels off the ground
Ball joint and tie rod play check

result.title: Fluid may be leaking onto the brakes at one wheel
result.now: Don't drive it. Have it towed or have a mechanic who comes to you check that wheel.
if: If the brake fluid reservoir is low, the leak is probably brake fluid. Brake failure is a real risk.
If the reservoir is full, the fluid may be gear oil or grease from an axle seal, which can still soak the pads and reduce braking on that side.
Don't try to clean the pads and drive on. Fluid-soaked pads usually can't be trusted, and a shop will find and fix the leak first.
result.why: Pads soaked with fluid lose much of their grip, so that wheel barely brakes and the car pulls toward the other side. If the fluid is brake fluid, the whole system can also lose pressure.

causes.name: Leaking brake caliper or wheel cylinder
causes.clues: Low brake fluid, a wet caliper or wet inside surface of the tire.

causes.name: Leaking brake hose or line
causes.clues: Fluid along a hose or line near the wheel.

causes.name: Axle seal or grease leak
causes.clues: Thick, dark, smelly oil on a rear wheel, with full brake fluid.

you: Check the brake fluid level under the hood.
Note which wheel is wet.
shop: Pad and shoe check for contamination

result.title: A brake pull needs a proper inspection to find the cause
result.now: Check your tire pressures, then get the brakes and steering inspected within the next few days.
if: If the pedal goes soft, the red brake light comes on, or you hear grinding, stop driving and have it towed.
If the pull is getting stronger, get it checked within a day or two.
If you smell burning or see smoke from a wheel, pull over, let it cool and don't drive further until it's checked.
result.why: A car that pulls when braking has an imbalance between the left and right side, in the brakes, tires or suspension. Most causes are straightforward to fix, but some get worse quickly, so it shouldn't wait long.

causes.name: Sticking caliper or uneven brakes
causes.clues: One wheel hotter or dustier than the others.

causes.name: Tire pressure or tire problem
causes.clues: One tire low or worn differently.

causes.name: Worn suspension or alignment
causes.clues: Clunks over bumps or an off-center steering wheel.

you: Check tire pressures.
Note which way it pulls and whether it happens on every stop.
